question: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 aimed at:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Promoting public sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 marked the beginning of economic planning in India, emphasizing the importance of public sector industries.
 
• It aimed to establish a mixed economy, where both public and private sectors would play a role in industrial development.
 
• The policy categorized industries into three groups: those exclusively managed by the state, those progressively managed by the state, and those left to private enterprises.
 
• Public sector industries were prioritized to ensure equitable resource distribution, reduce regional imbalances, and promote economic self-reliance.
 
• This resolution laid the foundation for India's industrialization and was a precursor to subsequent industrial policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mixed Economy Concept:** A mixed economy is an economic system combining private and public ownership of industries, aiming to balance efficiency and social welfare.
 
• **Public Sector Industries:** These are industries owned and operated by the government, focusing on key sectors like defense, railways, and heavy engineering.
 
• **Private Sector Role:** The private sector was encouraged to operate in areas where government intervention was not deemed necessary, fostering entrepreneurship.
 
• **Regional Imbalances:** The policy sought to reduce disparities in industrial development across different regions of the country.
 
• **Industrialization Strategy:** The resolution emphasized self-reliance and the development of heavy industries to accelerate economic growth and reduce dependency on foreign countries.
